issues.description: The problem statement and some comments refer to the feeding method using two different names: the UML and solution use messageOnFeed(), while several places in the textual tasks and descriptions refer to getFeedingSound(). This name/identifier mismatch between the specification and the explanatory text can confuse students about which method to implement and call (e.g. when implementing animals or when Farm.feedAllAnimals() should invoke it).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the problem statement and any template comments to reference messageOnFeed() (matching the UML and solution), or alternately rename the abstract method in the UML/solution to getFeedingSound() everywhere. Ensure the Farm.feedAllAnimals() description and any example code call the same method name students are expected to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the animal feeding method with two different identifiers: the UML and task spec declare an abstract method messageOnFeed(), while later parts of the written instructions (e.g. Part 2 and Part 3) refer to getFeedingSound(). The template/solution codebase uses messageOnFeed(). This mismatch can confuse students who will search for or try to implement getFeedingSound() based on the textual instructions even though the provided/expected code uses messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to consistently refer to messageOnFeed() wherever it currently mentions getFeedingSound(), or (B) rename the abstract method and all implementations in the template/solution from messageOnFeed() to getFeedingSound(). Prefer option (A) to match the current template/solution and avoid changing code used in tests.
